name: Midjourney
tagline: High-quality AI image generation with artistic coherence
description: Midjourney is widely regarded as the benchmark for artistic AI image generation, producing photorealistic and stylized images with strong composition and detail. It runs through Discord and a web app, with plans priced by GPU time rather than image count. There is no free tier or trial, so the cheapest way to test it is the Basic plan.

faqs.q: How much does Midjourney cost?
faqs.a: The Basic plan is $10 per month, or $8 per month billed annually, with Standard at $30, Pro at $60, and Mega at $120. Pricing is based on GPU time, not a fixed image count.

faqs.q: Does Midjourney have a free trial?
faqs.a: No. Midjourney removed its free trial in late 2024, so the cheapest way to test it is the $10 Basic plan.

faqs.q: How does Midjourney compare to Leonardo AI?
faqs.a: Midjourney leads on default aesthetic quality, while Leonardo AI offers a free tier and higher image volume per dollar. Heavy-volume users often prefer Leonardo.

faqs.q: Can you use Midjourney images commercially?
faqs.a: Yes. All paid plans include commercial usage rights, though companies earning over $1M a year must use the Pro or Mega plan.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Midjourney?
faqs.a: No free tier, GPU hours that do not roll over, and privacy (Stealth Mode) reserved for the $60 Pro plan and above.

name: Leonardo AI
tagline: AI image generation with high volume and free tier
description: Leonardo AI is a popular image generator known for high output volume, a usable free tier, style references, and a library of fine-tuned models for consistent results. Creators favour it for marketing and brand work where volume matters. Its default aesthetic is generally considered a step below Midjourney for purely artistic output.

faqs.q: How much does Leonardo AI cost?
faqs.a: Paid plans start around $12 per month, with higher tiers offering more daily tokens. There is also a free tier with daily credits.

faqs.q: Does Leonardo AI have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier provides daily credits, making it one of the more accessible ways to generate AI images without paying.

faqs.q: How does Leonardo AI compare to Midjourney?
faqs.a: Leonardo offers more images per dollar and a free tier, while Midjourney edges it on default artistic quality. Leonardo wins on value for high-volume work.

faqs.q: Is Leonardo AI good for brand consistency?
faqs.a: Yes. Its style references and fine-tuned model library help keep a consistent look across a campaign, which suits marketing creatives.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Leonardo AI?
faqs.a: Default output quality for purely artistic prompts trails Midjourney, and heavy use can exhaust the daily credit allocation quickly.

name: Ideogram
tagline: AI image generation that renders text accurately
description: Ideogram is an AI image generator best known for rendering readable text in images, which most rivals struggle with. That makes it a strong pick for logos, posters, and social graphics with words. It offers a free daily allowance, and pricing is generally cheaper than Midjourney, though its artistic range is narrower.

faqs.q: How much does Ideogram cost?
faqs.a: Ideogram has a free daily allowance, with paid plans starting in the $7 to $15 per month range depending on tier and image volume.

faqs.q: Is Ideogram free?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier includes a set number of image generations per day, enough to test its text-rendering strength.

faqs.q: Why is Ideogram good for text in images?
faqs.a: Its model is trained to render readable words. Put text in quotes in your prompt and it reliably appears, which beats Midjourney and DALL-E for signs, logos, and posters.

faqs.q: How does Ideogram compare to Midjourney?
faqs.a: Ideogram is cheaper and far better at text in images, while Midjourney produces more striking artistic output. Use each for its strength.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Ideogram?
faqs.a: Its artistic range is narrower than Midjourney, and some users report it can be inconsistent at following strict prompts for business use.

name: Recraft
tagline: AI design tool for vectors, logos, and brand assets
description: Recraft is an AI image and design tool aimed at editable brand assets like SVGs, logos, icons, posters, and mockups, with strong brand-consistency controls. It uses a credit system, with a free tier offering daily credits on public images. Paid plans unlock private images, commercial rights, and higher volume for professional design work.

faqs.q: How much does Recraft cost?
faqs.a: The Basic plan is $10 per month for 1,000 monthly credits, with Advanced at $27 and Pro at $48 for higher volume. A free tier offers 50 daily credits.

faqs.q: Does Recraft have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The free plan provides 50 daily credits, though images remain public and lack commercial rights until you upgrade.

faqs.q: What is Recraft best at?
faqs.a: Editable design assets. Recraft is strong for vector graphics, logos, icons, posters, and mockups rather than purely photographic images.

faqs.q: How does Recraft compare to Adobe Firefly?
faqs.a: Recraft is the better pick when the deliverable is an editable design asset like an SVG or logo, while Firefly suits teams working inside Creative Cloud.

faqs.q: Does Recraft offer commercial rights?
faqs.a: Yes, on paid plans. The free tier keeps images public without commercial rights, so brand work needs at least the Basic plan.

name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Commercially safe AI image, video, and audio generation
description: Adobe Firefly is a generative AI suite for images, video, audio, and vector graphics, built to be commercially safe and integrated across Photoshop, Illustrator, and Express. It uses a credit system and now offers access to partner models from Google, OpenAI, and Flux. It delivers less standalone value for users outside the Adobe ecosystem.

faqs.q: How much does Adobe Firefly cost?
faqs.a: The Standard plan is $9.99 per month for 2,000 credits, Pro is around $19.99 to $29.99, and Premium is $199.99 for 50,000 credits. A limited free tier exists.

faqs.q: Is Adobe Firefly free?
faqs.a: There is a free tier with limited monthly credits and watermarked output, suitable for testing. Paid plans remove watermarks and add credits.

faqs.q: Why choose Firefly over Midjourney?
faqs.a: Firefly is designed to be commercially safe and integrates directly with Photoshop, Illustrator, and Express, which matters for brand-governed production workflows.

faqs.q: Does Firefly do video and audio?
faqs.a: Yes. Firefly generates video and audio alongside images, and recent plans include access to partner models from Google, OpenAI, and Flux.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Adobe Firefly?
faqs.a: It offers less standalone value for users not already in the Adobe ecosystem, and the credit system needs watching on premium features.

name: Flux
tagline: Open-weight AI image models from Black Forest Labs
description: Flux is a family of AI image models from Black Forest Labs that became a developer favourite for near-Midjourney quality with open weights you can self-host. Access is mainly through the API or third-party platforms rather than a consumer subscription, with pricing charged per image. Casual users will find it less turnkey than hosted apps.

faqs.q: How much does Flux cost?
faqs.a: Flux is priced per image through its API, with Flux Pro reported at roughly $0.04 to $0.09 per image. Open weights can also be self-hosted for free if you have the hardware.

faqs.q: Is Flux free?
faqs.a: The open-weight models are free to run locally on capable hardware, but hosted API access is charged per image. There is no standard consumer subscription.

faqs.q: Is Flux open source?
faqs.a: Flux releases open-weight models, which is why developers favour it for self-hosting and custom pipelines, alongside a paid hosted API.

faqs.q: Who is Flux best for?
faqs.a: Developers and technical creators who want high image quality with control over hosting, rather than casual users who prefer a ready-made app.

faqs.q: How does Flux compare to Midjourney?
faqs.a: Flux can approach Midjourney quality and offers open weights and API access, while Midjourney is more turnkey with a polished interface but no self-hosting.

name: Runway
tagline: AI video generation with a full editing workstation
description: Runway is one of the most established AI video platforms, pairing its Gen-4 models with motion brush, green screen, inpainting, and timeline editing in one product. A single subscription now also routes to partner models like Veo and Kling. It is a strong all-rounder and a top Sora alternative for creators who want production workflow, not just generation.

faqs.q: How much does Runway cost?
faqs.a: Paid plans start around $12 to $15 per month for the Standard tier on annual billing, which unlocks Gen-4.5 plus integrated Veo and Kling models. A limited free tier exists.

faqs.q: Does Runway have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is limited. The free tier offers a small batch of credits and a few editor projects, enough to test the platform.

faqs.q: Is Runway a good Sora alternative?
faqs.a: Yes. With Sora being discontinued in 2026, Runway is a strong replacement for users who valued a production workflow, thanks to its integrated editor.

faqs.q: What makes Runway different from Pika or Kling?
faqs.a: Runway bundles a genuine editing suite, including motion brush, green screen, and inpainting, around the model, which saves hours of post-production.

faqs.q: Who is Runway best for?
faqs.a: Creators and agencies with post-production-heavy workflows who want generation and editing tools in one place rather than separate apps.

name: Kling AI
tagline: AI video generation with strong lip-sync and motion
description: Kling AI is a top-ranked AI video generator known for high-motion scenes, character animation, and accurate lip-sync, with native synchronized audio on its latest models. It offers commercial rights from its low entry tier and a limited free daily allowance. As a Sora alternative, it is among the most affordable routes to high-quality output.

faqs.q: How much does Kling AI cost?
faqs.a: Kling's entry paid plan starts around $6.99 per month and includes commercial rights, with higher Pro and Premier tiers for more credits and longer clips.

faqs.q: Does Kling AI have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier provides around 66 daily credits with no credit card required, enough for one to three test videos a day.

faqs.q: What is Kling AI best at?
faqs.a: High-motion scenes, character animation, and lip-sync. Its latest models also generate synchronized multi-language audio in a single pass.

faqs.q: Is Kling a good Sora alternative?
faqs.a: Yes. With Sora being discontinued in 2026, Kling offers one of the lowest-cost paths to high-quality AI video with commercial rights from the entry tier.

faqs.q: How does Kling compare to Runway?
faqs.a: Kling is cheaper per second of video and strong on motion, while Runway adds a full editing suite. Kling wins on price-to-quality for generation alone.

name: Pika
tagline: Fast AI video generation for short-form social clips
description: Pika is an AI video generator built for speed and short-form social content, with features like Pikaframes for image-to-image transitions and Pikaformance for lip-sync. It suits creators who value fast iteration and stylized effects over photorealism, and works well for vertical clips. Commercial rights and watermark-free exports require upgrading to the Pro tier.

faqs.q: How much does Pika cost?
faqs.a: Pika's Basic plan starts at $8 per month, with the Standard or Pro tier around $28 per month for commercial use and watermark-free exports.

faqs.q: Does Pika have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. Pika gives free credits on signup, though they expire, and free output carries limitations like watermarks.

faqs.q: What is Pika best at?
faqs.a: Fast, stylized short-form clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. Its PikaFrames feature generates transitions between a start and end image.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Pika?
faqs.a: Quality for complex prompts, photorealism, and character-driven scenes trails Runway, Kling, and Veo. Faces can distort on detailed prompts.

faqs.q: Do you need a paid plan for commercial use?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial rights and watermark-free exports require upgrading to the Pro tier, a detail that is easy to miss on the free plan.

name: Luma Dream Machine
tagline: AI video generation with high visual realism
description: Luma Dream Machine is an AI video generator from Luma Labs, recognized for high visual fidelity through its Ray models and a free tier for testing. Pricing is credit-based and scales with usage, and individual tiers include access to integrated third-party image and video models. Commercial rights require a paid plan.

faqs.q: How much does Luma Dream Machine cost?
faqs.a: Luma has a free tier with watermarked output, with paid plans starting around $10 per month and scaling by credits. Commercial rights require a paid plan.

faqs.q: Does Luma Dream Machine have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier includes limited credits with watermarked output, useful for testing quality before subscribing.

faqs.q: What is Luma best at?
faqs.a: Visual realism. Its Ray3 HDR model addresses the over-stylized look some creators notice in other generators, producing more photorealistic output.

faqs.q: Is Luma a good Sora alternative?
faqs.a: It is a reasonable option. With Sora being discontinued in 2026, Luma offers strong realism, though Runway and Veo are also worth comparing.

faqs.q: How does Luma compare to Runway?
faqs.a: Runway is more of a full editing studio, while Luma focuses on generation quality. Many creators use both together for different stages.

name: Google Veo
tagline: Google's AI video model with synchronized audio
description: Google Veo is a flagship AI video model known for cinematic realism and synchronized native audio, including dialogue and sound effects. Consumers access it through the Google AI subscription and Gemini, while businesses use it via Vertex AI with enterprise controls. It is one of the strongest Sora alternatives for realism and audio.

faqs.q: How much does Google Veo cost?
faqs.a: Consumer access comes through the Google AI Pro subscription at around $20 per month, which bundles Veo with Gemini. Business access via Vertex AI is priced separately.

faqs.q: Can you use Veo for free?
faqs.a: There is limited free access through the Gemini app, but consistent use of the Veo model requires the paid Google AI subscription.

faqs.q: What makes Veo stand out?
faqs.a: Synchronized native audio. Veo generates dialogue and sound effects alongside video, a capability shared by only a few top models in 2026.

faqs.q: Is Veo a good Sora alternative?
faqs.a: Yes. With Sora being discontinued in 2026, Veo is among the strongest replacements for cinematic realism with audio.

faqs.q: How do businesses access Veo?
faqs.a: Through Google's Vertex AI, which adds EU and US data residency controls and indemnification for outputs, suiting enterprise deployment.

name: HeyGen
tagline: AI avatar videos and voice cloning for creators
description: HeyGen creates talking-avatar videos from a script, with realistic lip-sync, voice cloning, and one-click translation across 175-plus languages. It suits marketing, social, and explainer content, and offers custom avatars from a short recording. Its credit system means real costs depend on usage, and credits do not roll over month to month.

faqs.q: How much does HeyGen cost?
faqs.a: The Creator plan is $24 per month on annual billing ($29 monthly) with unlimited video output and 200 credits. Higher Team and Scale tiers add more credits and features.

faqs.q: Does HeyGen have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier offers a small number of credits with watermarked output, designed for testing rather than production.

faqs.q: What is HeyGen best at?
faqs.a: Realistic talking-head avatar videos and translation. It supports 175-plus languages on paid plans and creates custom avatars from a short recording.

faqs.q: How does HeyGen compare to Synthesia?
faqs.a: HeyGen edges Synthesia on avatar realism and creator-friendly pricing, while Synthesia leads on enterprise features and LMS integration for corporate training.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of HeyGen?
faqs.a: Credits do not roll over, so a quiet month is wasted budget, and premium avatar features burn through credits faster than basic generation.

name: Synthesia
tagline: Enterprise AI avatar video for training and comms
description: Synthesia is the enterprise standard for AI avatar video, with 200-plus avatars, support for 140-plus languages, and a structured editor built for corporate training and communications. It prices by minutes per month, which teams find easier to budget than credits. There is no free plan, and custom avatars carry a substantial annual add-on fee.

faqs.q: How much does Synthesia cost?
faqs.a: The entry Personal or Starter plan is around $18 to $22 per month on annual billing, with the single-user Creator plan near $67 per month. Enterprise pricing is custom.

faqs.q: Does Synthesia have a free plan?
faqs.a: No permanent free plan. Synthesia offers a free trial, but production use requires a paid plan starting with Personal or Starter.

faqs.q: What is Synthesia best at?
faqs.a: Corporate training and communications at scale. It creates one video and can re-render it across many languages with matching lip-sync.

faqs.q: How does Synthesia compare to HeyGen?
faqs.a: Synthesia leads on enterprise features, LMS integration, and minute-based budgeting, while HeyGen is more flexible and creator-friendly at the entry tier.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Synthesia?
faqs.a: No free plan, and custom avatars carry an add-on fee of roughly $1,000 per year, which raises the real cost for branded presenters.

name: Suno
tagline: AI music generation with full vocals and stems
description: Suno is a top AI music generator that turns text prompts into complete songs with vocals, instrumentation, and mixing. Its Premier plan includes Suno Studio, an AI-native editor with multi-track timeline editing and stem export for further production. A free tier offers daily credits, though commercial rights require being a paid subscriber at the time of generation.

faqs.q: How much does Suno cost?
faqs.a: The Pro plan is $10 per month, or about $8 billed annually, with 2,500 credits. Premier is $30 per month for 10,000 credits and Suno Studio access. A free tier exists.

faqs.q: Is Suno free?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. The free tier gives around 50 daily credits, but tracks made on the free plan do not carry commercial rights even if you upgrade later.

faqs.q: What is Suno best at?
faqs.a: Complete, vocal-heavy songs. Suno excels at producing full tracks with lyrics, while rivals like Udio offer finer mixing control.

faqs.q: How does Suno compare to Udio?
faqs.a: Both start around $10 per month with similar credit structures. Suno leans toward finished vocal songs, Udio toward production control.

faqs.q: Do you get commercial rights with Suno?
faqs.a: Only on paid plans, and only for tracks generated while subscribed. Upgrading later does not grant retroactive rights to free-tier tracks.

name: Udio
tagline: AI music generation with fine production control
description: Udio is an AI music generator that competes directly with Suno, turning text prompts into full songs with a focus on mixing and production quality. Its pricing is simpler, with free credits to try it and a single main subscription unlocking most features. It recently increased credit allowances, making it generous on volume.

faqs.q: How much does Udio cost?
faqs.a: Udio's Standard plan is around $10 per month with roughly 2,400 credits, and the Pro tier is about $30 per month for higher volume. Free credits let you try it first.

faqs.q: Does Udio have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. Free credits let you test the platform, with a paid subscription unlocking extended generation and higher quality output.

faqs.q: What is Udio best at?
faqs.a: Production control and mixing quality. Udio gives finer control over the sound, while Suno leans toward complete vocal-heavy songs.

faqs.q: How does Udio compare to Suno?
faqs.a: Pricing is similar at around $10 per month. Udio recently boosted credits for more volume per dollar, while Suno is often preferred for finished songs.

faqs.q: Is Udio good value for hobbyists?
faqs.a: Yes. With simpler tiers and a $10 entry plan, Udio is often cited as the better value for people making music for fun.

name: PlayHT
tagline: AI voice generation and text-to-speech for creators
description: PlayHT is an AI voice platform offering realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning, and a large library of voices across many languages, aimed at creators producing voiceovers and narration. It also offers real-time voice APIs for developers. Pricing is usage-based, and the most natural voices and commercial use sit on paid tiers.

faqs.q: How much does PlayHT cost?
faqs.a: Paid plans start around $19 per month on annual billing for the Creator tier, with higher tiers for more characters and commercial use. Pricing is usage-based.

faqs.q: Does PlayHT have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. A free tier lets you test voices with limited characters, with paid plans unlocking commercial use and the most natural voices.

faqs.q: What is PlayHT best at?
faqs.a: Realistic voiceovers and narration. It offers a large voice library, voice cloning, and real-time voice APIs for developers building apps.

faqs.q: How does PlayHT compare to ElevenLabs?
faqs.a: Both offer high-quality AI voices and cloning. ElevenLabs is often cited as the voice-quality leader, while PlayHT competes on voice variety and developer APIs.

faqs.q: Who is PlayHT best for?
faqs.a: Creators producing voiceovers without recording, and developers needing text-to-speech or real-time voice in their own products.

name: Speechify
tagline: Text-to-speech for listening and voiceover creation
description: Speechify is a widely used text-to-speech app that reads documents, articles, and books aloud in natural AI voices across 60-plus languages, with a separate Studio product for voiceover creation. It serves students, professionals, and accessibility users. The free tier is limited, and some users report unexpected charges after trials, so cancellation timing matters.

faqs.q: How much does Speechify cost?
faqs.a: Premium is about $11.58 per month billed annually ($139 per year) or $29 monthly. Separate Studio plans for voiceover creation start around $19 per month.

faqs.q: Is Speechify free?
faqs.a: There is a free tier with 10 basic voices for casual use, but heavy readers and voiceover work need a paid plan.

faqs.q: What is Speechify best at?
faqs.a: Listening to written content. It converts documents, articles, and books into natural speech, which suits students and accessibility-focused users.

faqs.q: Does Speechify do voiceovers?
faqs.a: Yes, through its separate Studio product, which is aimed at creating voiceover audio rather than just reading text aloud.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Speechify?
faqs.a: The free tier is limited, and some users report unexpected post-trial charges, so set a reminder and verify limits before committing.

name: ChatGPT
tagline: The most widely used general-purpose AI assistant
description: ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose AI assistant and the most widely used chatbot, handling writing, research, coding, image generation, and voice. It offers a capable free tier plus paid plans for higher limits and advanced models. Creators use it for scripting, brainstorming, and repurposing content, though it can sometimes cite sources unreliably.

faqs.q: How much does ChatGPT cost?
faqs.a: ChatGPT has a free tier, with Go around $8, Plus at $20 per month, and Pro at roughly $100 to $200 for heavy users. Plus is the common paid entry point.

faqs.q: Is ChatGPT free?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier covers most everyday writing and research, with paid plans adding higher limits, advanced models, and more features.

faqs.q: What is ChatGPT best at?
faqs.a: Breadth. It handles conversation, creative tasks, coding, and general productivity, with extensive integrations, making it the most versatile assistant.

faqs.q: How does ChatGPT compare to Claude?
faqs.a: ChatGPT leads on breadth and ecosystem, while Claude is often preferred for coding depth and long-document writing. Many creators use both.

faqs.q: Can ChatGPT generate images?
faqs.a: Yes. Image generation is built in, so paid users can create visuals alongside text in the same conversation.

name: Claude
tagline: AI assistant strong in writing and reasoning
description: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant, recognized for clear reasoning, long-document handling, and high-quality writing and coding with fewer hallucinations than many rivals. It offers a free tier plus Pro and Max plans for higher usage. Creators use it for scripting, editing, and research, though it does not generate images like some general assistants.

faqs.q: How much does Claude cost?
faqs.a: Claude has a free tier, with Pro at $20 per month (about $17 on annual billing) and Max ranging from roughly $100 to $200 for heavy users.

faqs.q: Is Claude free?
faqs.a: Yes. The free tier covers everyday writing and research, with Pro adding higher usage limits and access to the most capable models.

faqs.q: What is Claude best at?
faqs.a: Reasoning, long-document analysis, and writing. It often produces clear, structured output and is frequently preferred for coding accuracy.

faqs.q: How does Claude compare to ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Claude is favoured for writing depth, long context, and coding precision, while ChatGPT offers broader features and built-in image generation.

faqs.q: Does Claude generate images?
faqs.a: No. Claude focuses on text, reasoning, and code rather than image generation, so creators needing visuals pair it with a separate tool.

name: Google Gemini
tagline: Google's multimodal AI assistant across its ecosystem
description: Google Gemini is Google's AI assistant and model family, working across text, image, audio, video, and code, and integrated into Search, Workspace, Android, and Chrome. It offers a free tier plus paid plans that add advanced models and the Veo video generator. Its strength is deep integration with Google's ecosystem.

faqs.q: How much does Google Gemini cost?
faqs.a: Gemini has a free tier, with the AI Pro plan at $19.99 per month and an AI Ultra tier around $100 to $200 for advanced features and higher limits.

faqs.q: Is Gemini free?
faqs.a: Yes. A free tier is available, with paid plans adding advanced models, higher limits, and access to the Veo video generator.

faqs.q: What is Gemini best at?
faqs.a: Ecosystem integration. Gemini works inside Search, Gmail, Docs, Android, and Chrome, which suits people already in Google's tools.

faqs.q: How does Gemini compare to ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Gemini shines inside Google Workspace and offers strong multimodal features, while ChatGPT leads on breadth and third-party integrations.

faqs.q: Does a Gemini subscription include video generation?
faqs.a: Yes. The Google AI Pro subscription bundles access to the Veo video model alongside the Gemini assistant.

name: Perplexity
tagline: AI search assistant that cites its sources
description: Perplexity is a research-focused AI assistant that combines a language model with real-time web retrieval, citing sources in its answers. The Pro plan routes queries across multiple frontier models rather than one provider. It is built for fact-checking and research, though it is weaker at coding and creative generation than general assistants.

faqs.q: How much does Perplexity cost?
faqs.a: Perplexity has a free tier, with Pro at $20 per month and a Max tier ranging higher for power users. Pro is the standard paid entry point.

faqs.q: Is Perplexity free?
faqs.a: Yes. The free plan covers basic AI search, with Pro adding advanced searches, a choice of models, and higher limits.

faqs.q: What is Perplexity best at?
faqs.a: Cited, up-to-date research. It pulls from the web and shows clickable sources, which suits fact-checking and learning.

faqs.q: How does Perplexity compare to ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Perplexity is search-native and source-cited, while ChatGPT is a broader generalist. Perplexity is the better pick for research and verification.

faqs.q: What is the biggest downside of Perplexity?
faqs.a: It is weaker at coding and creative generation than general assistants, so it works best alongside a tool like ChatGPT or Claude.

name: Grok
tagline: xAI's assistant with real-time X data access
description: Grok is xAI's AI assistant, distinguished by real-time access to X data, a large context window, and a less guarded conversational tone. It offers a free tier plus SuperGrok subscriptions and X Premium bundles. Creators use it for fast, current insights, though pricing across X and standalone plans can be confusing.

faqs.q: How much does Grok cost?
faqs.a: Grok has a free tier, with SuperGrok Lite around $10, SuperGrok at $30 per month ($300 a year), and a $300 monthly Heavy tier for maximum access.

faqs.q: Is Grok free?
faqs.a: Yes, but the free tier is throttled. SuperGrok at $30 per month is the cheapest standalone path to the full Grok experience.

faqs.q: What is Grok best at?
faqs.a: Real-time, current information. Its access to live X data and large context window suit fast-paced, insight-driven queries.

faqs.q: Do you need X Premium to use Grok?
faqs.a: No. X Premium bundles partial Grok access with social features, but SuperGrok is a separate, more capable AI subscription for less than Premium+.

faqs.q: How does Grok compare to ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Grok leans into real-time data and an informal tone, while ChatGPT offers more polished, reliable output and broader integrations.

name: DeepSeek
tagline: Open-source AI model with free web chat
description: DeepSeek is an open-source AI model from China offering frontier-class performance at a fraction of Western API costs, with a completely free web chat and no subscription tiers. Developers use its low-cost API for reasoning and coding. The major caveat is data storage in China, which has led several governments to restrict the app.

faqs.q: How much does DeepSeek cost?
faqs.a: The web chat is completely free with no subscription tiers. API access is charged per token at roughly one-tenth the cost of Western providers.

faqs.q: Is DeepSeek really free?
faqs.a: Yes. The chat at the DeepSeek site is free with no paywalls or ads, while developers pay low per-token rates for API use.

faqs.q: Is DeepSeek open source?
faqs.a: Yes. DeepSeek releases open models, which is why it is popular for budget deployments and self-hosting alongside its hosted chat.

faqs.q: What is the biggest concern with DeepSeek?
faqs.a: Data is stored in China, and the app has been banned or restricted by several governments, which matters for privacy-sensitive or business use.

faqs.q: How does DeepSeek compare to ChatGPT?
faqs.a: DeepSeek delivers competitive performance at far lower cost, but ChatGPT offers a more polished experience, broader features, and fewer data-residency concerns.
